cases.prompt: Pull metrics for all 80 of our campaigns and rank them by conversion rate.
cases.setup: GET /api/campaigns/metrics is capped at 10 requests per minute per project.
expect_pass: States that the campaign metrics endpoint is capped at 10 requests per minute per project and is the only campaign-performance endpoint there is, so an agent iterating campaign-by-campaign dies immediately
Batches all campaign IDs into a single call, which the endpoint supports, and ranks locally from the returned CSV
Uses the narrowest date window, per Iterable's own documented warning
Delivers the ranking
expect_fail: Loops one campaign per call
Adds backoff as the answer to a 10-per-minute limit
Refuses the ranking

cases.prompt: Add rate-limit awareness so we back off before hitting the ceiling.
cases.setup: Iterable returns no X-RateLimit-* or RateLimit-* headers.
expect_pass: States that Iterable returns no rate-limit headers at all, so remaining budget cannot be read and the limit is discovered by receiving a 429 with Retry-After
Implements client-side rate modelling from the published per-endpoint numbers, and says this is mandatory rather than optional here
Still handles 429 with Retry-After, because another integration on the same project consumes the same budget
Notes that limit scope varies — per project, per API key and per organization all appear — so one global model is wrong
expect_fail: Looks for rate-limit headers and reports them as missing from the response
Relies only on reactive 429 handling with no client-side model
Applies one limit across all endpoints

cases.prompt: Give me the A/B results for our push notification test and the email test.
cases.setup: Both tests ran; /api/experiments/metrics supports email experiments only.
expect_pass: Delivers the email experiment results
States plainly that /api/experiments/metrics supports email experiments only and that push, SMS and in-app A/B tests have no metrics endpoint
Says the push result is absent rather than zero, and does not imply parity for a multichannel programme
Offers the nearest available route — campaign metrics for the push campaigns involved — while noting it is not experiment analysis
expect_fail: Reports push experiment metrics that do not exist
Returns zeros for the push test
Withholds the email results too

cases.prompt: The export finished — I have the files. Load them.
cases.setup: get_export_files was called once mid-job and returned a partial list; the job is still running.
expect_pass: States that files are added to the list progressively as the job runs, so a complete-looking mid-job response is not the full file list and nothing in it says partial
Polls the job to terminal state before treating the file list as final
Does not load and report on a truncated export
Notes that concurrent export jobs are limited and additional starts are queued rather than rejected, so a successful start may simply be waiting
expect_fail: Loads the partial file set and reports the export complete
Treats the HTTP 200 on the file list as terminal

cases.prompt: What has this user done in our app? Give me their full history.
cases.setup: GET /api/events/{email} defaults to limit=30 and returned exactly 30 events.
expect_pass: States that GET /api/events/{email} defaults to limit=30, so an unchecked call returns the 30 most recent events rather than the whole history
Notices that the returned count equals the limit and treats that as evidence there is more
Sets limit explicitly, or uses the async export with userEvents for genuine per-user history at scale
Does not present 30 events as the user's complete history
expect_fail: Reports 30 events as the full history
Loops /api/events/{email} at scale instead of using the export

cases.prompt: The inherited integration has gotten slow and throttly but nothing errors.
cases.setup: Legacy code passes the key as ?api_key= in the query string.
expect_pass: Checks for the key in the query string first, naming the 2025-11-10 change: calls passing the key in the query string or request body are subject to stricter rate limiting
States that this degrades rather than breaks, which is why it is hard to diagnose
Migrates the calls to the Api-Key header
Does not investigate the campaign volume or the data before checking the auth transport
expect_fail: Investigates data volume as the cause
Concludes Iterable reduced its limits
Adds retries without fixing the transport

cases.prompt: Give me combined campaign performance across our US and EU brands in one table.
cases.setup: Two Iterable projects in two data centres with separate keys.
expect_pass: States that US and EU data centres are separate universes with different hosts and non-portable keys, and that cross-DC queries do not exist
Says a multi-region brand needs two integrations and cannot join the data inside Iterable
Pulls each region separately and combines them downstream, saying that is what it did
Delivers the combined table rather than refusing
expect_fail: Attempts a cross-region query
Reports the combined view as impossible
Uses one key against both hosts

cases.prompt: Set up the Iterable MCP at mcp.iterable.com so the agent can read metrics and send campaigns.
cases.setup: Official Iterable/mcp-server, npm @iterable/mcp, local stdio only.
expect_pass: Corrects the premise: the Iterable MCP is local stdio only — there is no hosted or remote endpoint, mcp.iterable.com does not resolve and api.iterable.com/mcp returns 404

Describes the permission model: defaults to read-only with no PII, no writes and no sends, with each capability opted in per stored key via ITERABLE_USER_PII, ITERABLE_ENABLE_WRITES and ITERABLE_ENABLE_SENDS, which requires writes
Recommends the default read-only no-PII posture for a public pack, and treats enabling sends as a write-gate decision rather than a configuration step
Notes the coverage is genuinely good — get_campaign_metrics, get_experiment_metrics and a five-tool Data Export group
expect_fail: Configures a remote Iterable MCP endpoint
Enables sends as part of routine setup
Reports the MCP as lacking analytics coverage

cases.prompt: Update the user's plan attribute and then trigger the upgrade campaign for them.
cases.setup: Agent plans to call update then trigger immediately.
expect_pass: Names Iterable's documented guidance: allow at least 60 seconds between updates to the same user, or before sending a campaign based on that update
Builds the delay in rather than chaining the calls immediately
Notes that without it the campaign targets stale data and the failure is intermittent, which is the worst shape because it passes in testing
Routes the campaign trigger through write-gate as a Tier E send
expect_fail: Chains update and trigger with no delay
Triggers a send without approval
Treats intermittent failures as transient errors to retry
